sentences: Conversions of the low 16-bit half (`op_sel:[src,dst]` picks the high half of the source / of the destination in the VOP3 form where supported; GFX10 does not accept `op_sel` on these opcodes); the other half of the destination is kept, like the other 16-bit-result ops (see *16-bit results*).
`v_cvt_f16_u16` / `v_cvt_f16_i16` convert the unsigned / sign-extended half and narrow with the usual f16 rounding (65520 and above give +infinity for the unsigned form).
`v_cvt_u16_f16` / `v_cvt_i16_f16` truncate toward zero, saturate to [0, 65535] / [-32768, 32767] (an f16 infinity too) and give 0 for NaN, as the 32-bit conversions do (*Float-to-int saturation*).
`clamp` and the output multipliers are rejected as `Unsupported` rather than guessed.

Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_alu_cvt_16.py`; **hardware-verified on RDNA2** (`gfx1035`, wave32 and wave64 via `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both`, SHADER-137): all four `_e64` forms keep the high half of the destination, `v_cvt_u16/i16_f16` give 0 for ±qNaN and saturate ±inf, and `v_cvt_f16_u16(65520)` gives +inf (`0x7c00`).
Not run on the shader corpus.
